correctness.rationale: A face is allowed iff at least one block has at most t vertices. The two resulting joins with one full simplex are contractible and meet in the join of the two (t−1)-skeleta; the inclusions are cofibrations, giving a suspension. Each skeleton is (t−2)-connected by the higher-dimensional cells of the full simplex, and its top reduced cycles are the kernel of augmentation contraction on the t-th exterior power. Splitting off any single vertex shows this kernel is canonically the t-th exterior power of the augmentation lattice and of rank binom(a−1,t) or binom(b−1,t), respectively. The graph case t=2 has the same wedge description by a spanning tree; higher cases use Hurewicz and Whitehead. The join and natural Mayer–Vietoris connecting map give the stated integral tensor. Under block exchange the connecting map has a negative sign from reversing the ordered cover, and switching t vertices with t gives (−1)^(t²); their product is (−1)^(t+1). Equal weights on matched pairs identify the actual fixed locus PL with the allowed orbit-size skeleton. After barycentric subdivision the quotient cellular chains are coinvariants, which are exact over Q by averaging, so the flip trace and the claimed rank formula apply to the genuine quotient. At n=t+1 radial projection from the barycenter of the full-simplex boundary gives the unit sphere in the sum-zero representation, with + and − real dimensions t and t+1. Its quotient is precisely the join with RP^t; the t-fold homology shift carries H1(RP^t)=Z/2 to degree t+1 for every t≥2.
residual_risks: The bundled finite tests check mod-two Betti ranks and Lefschetz traces, not the full integral module or quotient torsion; the proof supplies those.

value.rationale: The family is a natural tolerance construction and the result classifies its integral symmetry action rather than only counting spheres. The sign distinguishes parity in the rational quotient ranks, and the smallest genuine quotient already carries integral torsion absent in the original space. The explicit fixed-locus and chain descriptions make this a usable example of why invariant rational homology cannot substitute for integral geometric quotient topology.
residual_risks: Value concerns two disjoint blocks; larger balanced integral quotients and multiblock variants are outside the claim.
